title: Karaage
subtitle: Japanese fried chicken
excerpt: Karaage is bite-size chicken thigh marinated in soy, ginger and sake, then coated in cornflour and fried until deeply crispy. It is one of the most popular dishes in Japan. Serves 4.
sourceNotes: Karaage developed in Japan in the mid-20th century as a popular home cooking dish. The cornflour coating and the double-fry method give it a crust that stays crispy longer than Western fried chicken.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Marinate up to 8 hours ahead in the fridge. Fry just before serving.
recipe.temperatureNote: Oil temperature for frying. Use a thermometer to maintain consistent heat.

glossaryTerms.definition: A Japanese technique of marinating protein in soy and ginger, then frying in cornflour for a very crispy, light crust.
Very fine white starch ground from maize. Used in karaage for a thinner, crispier crust than plain flour.

content.text: instead of plain flour, and frying twice. The first fry cooks the chicken through at a lower heat. The second fry at higher heat crisps the coating.
Chicken thigh is essential here. Breast dries out too quickly in the hot oil and does not absorb the marinade as well.

items.prepNote: boneless, skin on, cut into 4cm pieces

content.text: Combine the soy sauce, sake, ginger, garlic and sesame oil in a bowl. Add the chicken pieces and mix well. Leave to marinate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 8 hours in the fridge.
Heat the oil in a wok to 160C. While the oil heats, toss the marinated chicken in the cornflour and press to coat well.
Fry the chicken in batches for 3 to 4 minutes until cooked through but only lightly golden. Remove with tongs and drain on a rack.
Raise the oil temperature to 180C. Return the chicken to the oil in batches and fry for 1 to 2 minutes until deeply golden and very crispy.
Drain on the rack for 1 minute and serve immediately with wedges of lemon and Japanese mayonnaise if you like.

attrs.symptom: Coating is pale and soft, not crispy
attrs.cause: Oil temperature dropped during frying or the second fry was skipped
attrs.fix: Fry in small batches and always do the second high-heat fry. Never crowd the wok.

attrs.cause: Breast meat was used instead of thigh
attrs.fix: Always use boneless chicken thigh. The fat content keeps it moist through two fries.

attrs.symptom: Coating falls off in the oil
attrs.cause: Chicken was not drained of excess marinade before coating in cornflour
attrs.fix: Let excess marinade drip off before tossing in cornflour. Press the coating on firmly.

content.text: Karaage appears everywhere in Japan. It is a staple of bento boxes, izakaya menus, convenience stores and school canteens. Home cooks fry it fresh for weeknight dinners. The double-fry method is also used for other fried foods across Japanese cooking. Once you learn this technique, the results are noticeably better than any single fry.
